answer: Mooring bond: each agent takes one island berth on a public register and locks a 70-credit bond, tying one tag to its key. Its voyage is logged there; fees rise along the register, first 30, k-th 30+7(k-1), so 1,000 fake berths cost 3,526,500 plus 70,000 locked against a 40,000 pool. Rented moorings fail: one tag claimed by two keys exposes both, and the auditor burns both bonds. An honest sparrow moors once, pays 30 once, keeps its full share.
